question: What is the main goal of the intersectoral team approach in health?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on hospital-based curative medical treatments
options.B: Merging all government ministries into a single large health department
options.C: Coordinating different sectors to address broader health determinants
options.D: Eliminating the need for traditional hospitals and clinics

explanation: The intersectoral approach looks beyond medicine to unite various societal sectors for better community health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h1)

question: Why must primary health care involve agencies outside the health sector?

options.A: Health outcomes are heavily influenced by social and economic factors
options.B: International donors refuse to fund standalone medical programs
options.C: Ministries of health have excess funds to share with other departments
options.D: Medical doctors lack the time to handle community sanitation duties

explanation: Factors like clean water, education, and food security directly impact disease rates and require non-health sector intervention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h1)

question: A community-focused health program ensures local people help plan activities. Which principle does this represent?
explanation: Involving local residents in decision-making reflects the core principle of participation in primary health care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h2)

question: What does the principle of equity mean in intersectoral health planning?

options.A: Giving priority to wealthy urban centers with better tax compliance
options.B: Dividing government funds equally among all registered political wards
options.C: Ensuring every ministry receives an identical budget allocation
options.D: Directing resources to the most vulnerable groups who need them most

explanation: Equity focuses on fairness by addressing disparities and directing extra support to disadvantaged populations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h2)

question: Which sector is primarily responsible for improving rural food security and nutrition?
explanation: Agricultural ministries and farmers directly influence food availability, dietary diversity, and nutritional status. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h3)

question: How does the education sector directly support community health goals?

options.A: By supplying free pharmaceutical drugs to local dispensaries
options.B: By teaching personal hygiene and health literacy to young people
options.C: By diagnosing common tropical diseases during school hours
options.D: By constructing modern primary healthcare clinics in rural areas

explanation: Schools serve as vital hubs for instilling healthy habits and health knowledge in the younger generation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h3)

question: What is a primary function of the community health nurse in multisectoral teams?

options.A: Acting as a bridge between the health sector and community groups
options.B: Constructing boreholes and rural water supply systems
options.C: Managing financial budgets for the Ministry of Agriculture
options.D: Handling court cases related to sanitation law violations

explanation: Nurses connect clinical health services with community resources and other development sectors. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h4)

question: A community health nurse notices rising malnutrition rates in a rural village. What is the most appropriate collaborative action?

options.A: Refer every single child immediately to a tertiary teaching hospital
options.B: Wait for the federal government to distribute free food parcels
options.C: Partner with agricultural and education sectors to promote local food production
options.D: Close down all local markets until families start buying imported supplements

explanation: Addressing malnutrition requires working with food producers and educators rather than relying solely on clinical treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h4)

question: What helps prevent misunderstandings among different sectors working on a joint project?

options.A: Punishing agencies that miss internal deadlines
options.B: Clear terms of reference and regular joint meetings
options.C: Relying entirely on informal word-of-mouth messages
options.D: Strict isolation of each department from the others

explanation: Structured meetings and explicit role definitions ensure all participating agencies stay coordinated and focused. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h5)

question: Why do different government agencies sometimes struggle to work together?

options.A: Bureaucratic rivalries and differing institutional priorities
options.B: All civil servants speak completely different foreign languages
options.C: Health workers have legal authority over all other ministries
options.D: They share the exact same financial budgets and resources

explanation: Each sector often has its own mandates, funding streams, and targets, which can hinder seamless cooperation. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h5)

question: What is a major consequence of institutional silos in government ministries?

options.A: Rural communities receive an excess of duplicated services
options.B: Agencies fail to share data and resources effectively
options.C: Healthcare workers take over agricultural extension duties
options.D: Ministries merge automatically to save operational costs

explanation: Silos cause departments to work in isolation, preventing the pooling of resources needed for holistic health programs. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h6)

question: Which factor frequently disrupts ongoing intersectoral partnerships in the public sector?

options.A: Universal agreement on primary healthcare budgets
options.C: An excess of trained community health nurses

explanation: Constant changes in administrative leadership break continuity and stall collaborative momentum. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h6)

question: What ensures a community health program continues after external funding stops?

options.A: Passing strict laws that criminalize poor hygiene
options.B: Complete dependence on foreign donor agencies
options.C: Handing full control over to private pharmaceutical companies
options.D: Genuine community ownership and local involvement

explanation: When locals feel a program belongs to them, they maintain it independently of external support. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)

question: Why is it important to track non-medical indicators in an intersectoral health program?

options.A: Ministries of health refuse to look at hospital admission logs
options.B: Health is influenced by broader social factors like education and income
options.C: Medical indicators are considered unreliable by international researchers
options.D: Clinics lack the computer software to record standard medical diagnoses

explanation: Tracking educational or agricultural metrics captures the wide-ranging impact of multisectoral interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)
